papers.title: Three-Dimensional Refractive Index Patterns Distinguish CD57-Defined Subsets of Human Memory T Cells
papers.abstract: Distinguishing T-cell subsets is important for characterizing immune differentiation, but label-free classification is challenging because closely related subsets have overlapping biophysical properties. We combined holotomography with a three-dimensional convolutional neural network to classify primary human T cells from their refractive index (RI) tomograms. Fluorescence-activated cell sorting defined four reference populations: CD4+, naive CD8+, and CD57- and CD57+ memory CD8+ T cells. The FishNet-inspired classifier achieved 97.04% accuracy in a cell-level held-out test of 270 cells. Dedicated binary classifiers achieved 97.70% accuracy for naive versus CCR7- memory CD8+ cells and 94.44% for CD57- versus CD57+ memory CD8+ cells. Although the memory subsets overlapped in whole-cell descriptors, their volumetric RI patterns supported classification. These findings establish a basis for investigating intrinsic optical phenotypes associated with CD57-defined T-cell differentiation.

papers.title: Biphasic glycocalyx remodelling balances immune cell recruitment and tissue damage during influenza infection
papers.abstract: The endothelial glycocalyx is a glycan-rich barrier lining blood vessels that regulates immune cell recruitment, whose role in viral infection is unknown. Using a murine influenza model, we reveal that the lung endothelial glycocalyx undergoes coordinated biphasic remodelling: early shedding followed by substantial accumulation during peak immune activation. Genetic deletion of heparanase, the enzyme driving early glycocalyx shedding, reduced immune cell lung infiltration and improved host recovery. Conversely, using a new endothelial-specific glycocalyx depletion mouse model, we demonstrate that this glycocalyx accumulation actively limits immune cell recruitment and prevents excessive tissue damage. Together, these findings reveal that coordinated endothelial and immune cell glycocalyx remodelling is an active and previously unrecognised regulator of the balance between antiviral immune cell recruitment and tissue protection.

papers.title: The decidual microenvironment shapes neutrophil subsets that promote extravillous trophoblast invasion in early pregnancy
papers.abstract: Successful establishment of the maternal-fetal interface is a critical process during early pregnancy, ensuring healthy fetal development. A critical phase in establishing the utero-placental blood supply is the invasion of extravillous trophoblasts (EVTs) into the maternal spiral arteries, marking the transformation of the endometrium into the decidua. By separating the EVT invaded decidua (iDec) and EVT non-invaded decidua (niDec), we demonstrate that neutrophils dominate the iDec immune landscape during early human pregnancy. High-dimensional flow cytometry and single-cell transcriptomics revealed that the decidualized microenvironment extends neutrophil survival and shapes discrete tissue-resident subsets, including an activated CD63high phenotype. Imaging mass cytometry uncovered a precise spatial organization, demonstrating preferential cell-cell interactions between these activated neutrophils and invading EVTs. Furthermore, functional in vitro assays demonstrated that the neutrophil secretome, including the core granular protease neutrophil elastase, directly stimulates EVT invasion. Together, these findings identify decidua-associated neutrophils as crucial cellular coordinators of human placental development.

papers.title: Spatially-Organized Adaptive Immune Niches in Granulomas Dictate Local Defense and Correlate with Disease Severity in Tuberculosis Patients
papers.abstract: The cellular composition and spatial organization of immune responses within tuberculosis (TB) granulomas have been increasingly characterized, yet how these spatially organized immune cell populations coordinate local adaptive immunity remains largely unknown. Here, we integrated single-cell multi-omics, spatial transcriptomics, and immune receptor profiling to construct a comprehensive spatial atlas of human TB granulomas. We identified two concentric adaptive immune niches surrounding the central necrotic core. The outer niche comprised granuloma-associated tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) that supported TFH-B cell interactions and exhibited functional germinal center-like features associated with antigen-driven B-cell maturation toward FCRL5 antibody-producing cells. The inner niche contained antigen-experienced and Mtb-reactive effector memory CD8 T cells (TEM), which were recruited from distal lung regions by LGALS9high chemokine-expressing macrophages and activated to undergo local clonal expansion. In lgals9l1 deficient zebrafish, macrophage depletion was accompanied by marked reductions in T- and B-cell enrichment within granulomas and increased bacterial loads, supporting a role for LGALS9high macrophages in coordinating local adaptive immunity against TB infection. Finally, AI-based prediction of spatial gene expression from clinical hematoxylin and eosin-stained specimens revealed that inferred TLS abundance increased with TB disease severity. These findings identify spatially interconnected adaptive immune niches that organize protective immune responses within human TB granulomas, therefore providing a foundation for understanding granuloma adaptive immunity and developing host-directed therapies and vaccines for TB (https://tbomics.smart-nbc.org.cn/).

papers.title: Intestinal goblet cell loss induces microbiota-independent mucosal and systemic IgA dysregulation
papers.abstract: Goblet cells are essential for establishing the intestinal mucus layer and exert diverse immunomodulatory functions. The mucus barrier cooperates with secretory immunoglobulin A (IgA) to regulate host-microbiota interactions and maintain intestinal immune homeostasis. The extent to which goblet cells directly regulate IgA responses remains unclear. Here, we show that depletion of Muc2-expressing intestinal secretory cells in mice caused barrier dysfunction and intestinal inflammation accompanied by profound mucosal and systemic IgA dysregulation, including hyper-IgA, circulating IgA-IgG immune complexes and renal IgA deposition. Selective Paneth cell depletion did not reproduce these IgA abnormalities, and Muc2-deficient mice showed an intermediate phenotype, implicating loss of goblet-cells rather than Paneth cells or of Muc2 loss in this phenotype. Germ-free rederivation markedly attenuated intestinal inflammation but did not prevent mucosal and systemic hyper-IgA or IgA-IgG immune-complex formation, demonstrating that goblet cell loss drives IgA dysregulation independently of live microbial colonisation. Goblet cell loss and IgA deficiency shaped the mucosa-associated microbiota largely independently, as goblet cell depletion promotes expansion of the genus Akkermansia, whereas IgA deficiency reduced Akkermansia but allowed expansion of Mucispirillum and aggravated colonic pathology, indicating that elevated IgA response is partially protective. These findings reveal goblet cells as critical regulators of mucosal and systemic IgA homeostasis beyond mucus production and point to epithelial-immune interactions as potential contributors to IgA-mediated diseases.

papers.title: Label-Free Lymphocyte Subtype and State Classification by Stimulated Raman Scattering Microscopy
papers.abstract: Accurate immune cell subtype and functional state profiling are essential for studying immune regulation, disease progression, and therapeutic response. Established single-cell analysis techniques rely heavily on either endpoint, destructive measurements or complex labeling that can potentially affect cell functions. Stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy offers quantitative, label-free imaging of cells and tissues by providing contrast based on subcellular concentrations of intrinsic biomolecules at high spatial and temporal resolution. Here, we demonstrate that Vision Transformer based hyperspectral SRS imaging classification can accurately and non-destructively classify various lymphocyte phenotypes, including lymphocyte lineage (T and B cells), T cell subset and differentiation state (CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, effector, memory, and naive for both), and functional states (naive T, activated T, exhausted T) using fluorescent markers for training. By leveraging attention-based spatial-spectral feature learning, the approach captures biomolecular patterns associated with immune cell identity and state while preserving cells for downstream or longitudinal analysis. This provides a potential platform for label-free immune profiling, live-cell analysis, and longitudinal studies of immune cell type and state transitions.

papers.title: Seroprotection and improved polyfunctional immunity conferred by a YF17D-vectored rabies vaccine
papers.abstract: Rabies remains a major public-health challenge, with pre-exposure vaccination strategies constrained by the need for multiple doses and repeated healthcare visits. Here we describe YF-RabG, a live-attenuated rabies vaccine candidate based on the yellow fever 17D (YF17D) vaccine backbone that stably expresses the rabies virus glycoprotein (RabG). YF-RabG exhibited an attenuated phenotype and favourable safety profile compared with parental YF17D across several preclinical models, including neonatal and immunocompromised mice. A single immunization induced robust humoral and cell-mediated immune responses in non-human primates. Rabies virus-neutralizing antibody titres readily exceeded the widely accepted correlate of protection in mice, hamsters and non-human primates by several orders. Accordingly, vaccination conferred protection against lethal rabies challenge in a range of stringent mouse models, maintained seroprotective antibody levels for at least one year, and increased following a boost using a licensed rabies vaccine. Furthermore, the YF17D vector was readily adapted to accommodate glycoproteins from distant lyssaviruses, generating protective vaccine candidates against Mokola, Lagos bat and Lleida bat lyssaviruses. Collectively, these findings identify YF-RabG as a promising single-dose rabies vaccine candidate and highlight the versatility of the YF17D platform for lyssavirus vaccine development.

papers.title: C3-targeting siRNA Combined with Oseltamivir Alleviates Inflammation and Lung Injury in H1N1-Infected Mice
papers.abstract: Influenza A H1N1 infection can trigger severe inflammatory responses that contribute to pulmonary tissue injury and disease progression. Aberrant complement activation is presumed to contribute to these pathological changes. Nevertheless, it remains unclear whether complement C3 serves as a shared upstream regulatory node linking inflammation and hemolytic injury. In this study, we established an H1N1-infected mouse model to dynamically monitor changes in inflammation, hemolysis and complement-related parameters throughout infection. We evaluated the C3-silencing efficacy of RG002, a liver-targeted siRNA against complement C3, as well as the therapeutic efficacy of RG002 combined with oseltamivir against H1N1 infection. Our results showed that H1N1 infection induced prominent inflammatory responses and alterations in peripheral blood cell parameters, accompanied by pulmonary histopathological injury in mice. Hepatic C3 expression and complement activity were simultaneously and markedly elevated. RG002 suppressed C3 expression in a dose-and time-dependent manner and reduced complement-mediated erythrocyte lysis in serum. In vivo therapeutic experiments demonstrated that on the basis of viral replication suppression achieved by oseltamivir, combination treatment with RG002 inhibited excessive complement activation. This combined regimen reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine levels, attenuated pulmonary histopathological injury, and improved selected peripheral blood cell parameters. Notably the low-dose RG002 combination group exhibited superior performance across multiple evaluation indices, suggesting that the degree of C3 suppression is preferable to influence therapeutic effucaty. Collectively, our findings implicate complement C3 in the inflammatory pathology associated with H1N1 infection and demonstrate the therapeutic potential of C3-targeting siRNA as an adjunct to antiviral treatment. This study provides experimental evidence supporting the combination of antiviral therapy and controlled complement modulation as a potential host-directed therapeutic strategy for severe influenza.

papers.title: From Adalimumab to orally administered secretory IgA: preclinical characterization of ABC-301
papers.abstract: Reformatting therapeutic immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies into secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA) may provide an alternative architecture for mucosal drug delivery. We characterized ABC-301, a recombinant human sIgA1 incorporating the antigen-binding regions of Adalimumab, and evaluated its human tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF) neutralization, oral activity in experimental colitis, tissue biodistribution, and susceptibility to patient-derived anti-Adalimumab antibodies. ABC-301 retained human TNF binding and functional neutralization in vitro. Its whole-molecule molar neutralization IC50 was approximately 3.3-fold lower than that of Adalimumab, a difference of approximately 1.6-fold after normalization to theoretical binding-site number. In dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis, oral ABC-301 attenuated colon shortening and reduced colonic inflammatory myeloid populations and tissue inflammatory biomarkers relative to untreated DSS controls. Following oral administration, iodine-125-associated radioactivity was predominantly detected in gastrointestinal compartments. In seven patient-derived anti-Adalimumab antibody preparations, ABC-301 showed reduced functional susceptibility to inhibition compared with Adalimumab. These findings provide a preclinical proof of concept for IgG-to-sIgA reformatting.

papers.title: In vitro and in vivo validation of recombinant Syrian hamster interferon-α
papers.abstract: The Syrian hamster (Mesocricetus auratus) is an important model for the study of viral pathogenesis and the development of antiviral drugs and vaccines, yet species-specific reagents remain scarce. Here, we validate the potent and specific activity of recombinantly expressed Syrian hamster maIFN-12-like protein (maIFN) in vitro and in vivo. MaIFN expressed in E. coli induced MX2 and ISG15 expression in both BHK21 hamster kidney cells as well as in primary hamster fibroblasts in a dose-dependent manner and EC50 values in low pg/mL range. Activation was strictly STAT2-dependent and more potent, by at least one order of magnitude, than that achieved by heterologous human or mouse IFN. ISG induction translated into a strong antiviral activity against YF17D virus replication in BHK21 cells as well as ISRE-dependent reporter expression in a newly established hamster reporter cell line. When tested in wild-type but not in STAT2-deficient hamsters, maIFN showed a physiologic, vigorous yet rapidly contracting systemic ISG response. Together these findings establish maIFN as a functional antiviral cytokine and valuable reagent for preclinical infectious disease research using Syrian hamsters.

papers.title: Prim-O-glucosylcimifugin suppresses M2 macrophage polarization via the JAK2-STAT6-PPARγ pathway to alleviate allergic asthma
papers.abstract: Background: Allergic asthma (AA) is a chronic respiratory disease closely linked to immune-inflammatory responses driven by M2 macrophage polarization. PrimO-glucosylcimifugin (POG), a natural bioactive compound from Saposhnikovia divaricata (SD), alleviates inflammation in acute lung injury mice, but whether it mitigates AA by modulating M2 macrophage polarization remains unclear. Objective: This study investigated POGs effects on AA and its mechanisms in regulating M2 macrophage polarization. Methods: LC-MS profiled the SD/Prunus mume (PM) combination, and network pharmacology predicted its main active components and key anti-AA mechanisms. Ovalbumin (OVA) plus IL-4 established AA models in mice and RAW264.7 cells. Lung protection was assessed by histopathology, lung indices, and type II immune inflammatory cytokine markers. Flow Cytometry, RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence, and Western blot examined key genes/proteins in the JAK2-STAT6-PPAR{gamma} axis. Results: LC-MS-based network pharmacology identified POG as the key SD/PM active ingredient alleviating AA. Pharmacodynamic evaluation showed POG effectively alleviated OVA-induced airway inflammation and pulmonary histopathological damage in AA mice. Mechanistically, POG inhibited M2 macrophage polarization by downregulating key JAK2-STAT6-PPAR{gamma} axis factors. Conclusion: POG ameliorates AA by reducing type II immune factor release through JAK2-STAT6-PPAR{gamma}-mediated inhibition of M2 macrophage polarization. This study clarifies POGs anti-AA mechanism and supports its clinical development.

papers.title: Acute hypertension causes focal coronary artery perivascular cGAS-, IRF3, and IFNAR-dependent type I interferon responses
papers.abstract: Hypertension exposes coronary arteries to dynamic mechanical forces that alter the structural integrity and lead to pathologic changes such as aneurysm, dissection, or atherogenesis. Although the effects of chronic hypertension have been extensively studied, the early molecular responses to increased luminal pressure remain poorly understood. Here, we find that acute hypertension in murine coronary arteries induced by transverse aortic constriction (TAC) causes focal perivascular type I interferon (IFN) responses in the vessel wall in contrast to comparatively homogeneous perivascular fibrosis. Spatial transcriptomics and RNAscope independently demonstrate spatially clustered expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in the walls of pressurized left and right coronary arteries in the first week after TAC. Genetic disruption of cGAS or IRF3 each markedly attenuated the perivascular ISG response, indicating the response is a consequence of DNA sensing. Pharmacologic disruption of type I IFN signaling using an anti-IFNAR antibody abolished pressure-induced induction of focal ISG expression suggesting the pathway can be inhibited therapeutically. Since focal type I IFN signaling in the infarct borderzone of the left ventricle increased risk of dilation and rupture, we propose that focal perivascular type I IFN signaling in the vessel wall may serve as a nidus for analogous pathologies like aneurysm, dissection, or atherogenesis and represent a potential target for therapy.

papers.title: SIRT3 preserves mitochondrial DNA integrity to restrain cGAS-STING signaling and autoimmune inflammation
papers.abstract: Mitochondria play critical roles beyond energy production, including regulation of innate immunity through release of damage-associated molecular patterns such as mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA). Sirtuin 3 (SIRT3), a mitochondrial deacetylase, modulates mitochondrial function, reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, and inflammation. Here, we investigate the role of SIRT3 in controlling Type I interferon (IFN) responses in macrophages. We show that Sirt3 depletion in mouse macrophages increases basal mtDNA release into the cytosol, activating the cGAS-STING pathway and enhancing the expression of IFN-{beta} and downstream interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs). Accordingly, Sirt3-deficient cells exhibit markedly increased resistance to vesicular stomatitis virus infection. Secreted IFN-{beta} also acts in a paracrine manner, priming neighboring cells and reinforcing antiviral defenses. Using mtDNA-deficient ({rho}0) cells, we demonstrate that intact mtDNA is essential for this amplified interferon response, as mtDNA depletion abolishes IFN-{beta} induction following Sirt3 knockdown. Mechanistically, increased mitochondrial ROS (mtROS) in SIRT3-deficient cells promotes mtDNA leakage and cGAS-STING activation, effects that are attenuated by the mitochondrial superoxide scavenger MitoTEMPO. In vivo, SIRT3 protects against chlorhexidine gluconate-induced peritoneal fibrosis by restraining macrophage infiltration, ISGs expression and fibrotic remodeling, underscoring its role in modulating STING-dependent inflammation and tissue damage. Finally, reanalysis of transcriptomic datasets from patients with lupus nephritis and rheumatoid arthritis reveals reduced SIRT3 expression, suggesting that SIRT3 downregulation is also associated with human inflammatory diseases. Collectively, our findings identify SIRT3 as an important regulator of mitochondrial integrity and oxidative stress that modulates innate immune and antiviral responses.

papers.title: Macaque Vγ4+ γδ T cells exhibit distinct IFN-γ and IL-22 effector profiles that are dysregulated during chronic SIV infection and diarrheal disease
papers.abstract: V{gamma}4+ {gamma}{delta} T cells contribute to colonic homeostasis in humans, but their biology in nonhuman primates remains poorly defined. Here, we characterized V{gamma}4+ {gamma}{delta} T cells in blood and intestinal tissues of healthy, diarrhea-inflicted, and SIV-infected rhesus macaques. TRG/TRD repertoire sequencing across colon, mesenteric lymph node, blood, and spleen revealed compartment-specific clonal architecture and colonic enrichment of TRGV3. Flow cytometric profiling revealed circulating and colonic V{gamma}4+ T cells were predominantly V{delta}1+, exhibited an effector memory phenotype, and displayed T-bet-dominant transcriptional profiles. High-dimensional clustering confirmed V{gamma}4+V{delta}1+ T cells as a distinct terminally differentiated lineage. Functionally, stimulated V{gamma}4+ T cells exhibited robust Th1/Th17 cytokine production, supporting dual inflammatory and barrier-protective roles. Campylobacter-associated diarrhea was characterized by mucosal expansion of central memory V{gamma}4+ T cells and altered cytokine responses. In contrast, ART-suppressed chronic SIV infection was associated with colonic enrichment of naive-like V{gamma}4+ T cells and increased ROR{gamma}t expression, alongside profound systemic loss of cytokine production but relative preservation of mucosal Th17-type responses. Both conditions exhibited a convergent loss of systemic Type 1 effector V{gamma}4+ T-cell responses, pointing to a shared functional alteration during chronic intestinal inflammation. Overall, these findings reveal disease-specific remodeling of V{gamma}4+ T cells during chronic intestinal inflammation and gut barrier disruption in chronic enterocolitis and SIV infection.

papers.title: Nicotinamide Riboside Attenuates inflammation in a mouse model of psoriasis
papers.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease driven by dysregulated immune responses, in which IL-17-producing T cells play a central role. Nicotinamide riboside (NR), a precursor of NAD+, has recently emerged as a potential immunomodulatory intervention. Previous studies have shown that NR preferentially suppresses Th17 responsiveness in CD4+ T cells from individuals with psoriasis, but whether NR can attenuate psoriasiform inflammation in vivo remains poorly defined. Here, we investigated the effects of NR supplementation in a mouse model of imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasiform skin inflammation. NR treatment markedly attenuated IMQ-induced splenomegaly and reduced epidermal thickening, indicating an improvement of both systemic and cutaneous inflammatory manifestations. Flow cytometric analysis of skin infiltrates revealed a reduction in inflammatory myeloid populations, including neutrophils and inflammatory monocyte-macrophages, together with a pronounced decrease in dermal TCR {gamma}{delta} and CD4+ T cells. Consistent with these findings, CD4+ T cells isolated from IMQ-treated mice displayed increased IL-17A production following ex vivo TCR stimulation, which was significantly reduced by NR supplementation in a dose-dependent manner. IFN{gamma} and IL-4 responses were not significantly altered by NR in this setting. Furthermore, NR suppressed IL-17A production in Th17-polarized CD4+ T cells, while leaving Th1 and Th2 responses largely unaffected. Together, these findings show that NR treatment attenuates IMQ-induced psoriasiform skin inflammation in vivo and preferentially modulates IL-17A-associated CD4 T-cell responses. The accompanying reduction in dermal {gamma}{delta} T-cell numbers suggests that NR may also influence innate-like T-cell populations involved in cutaneous inflammation, providing experimental evidence for NAD+ boosting as a potential immunomodulatory strategy in psoriasis.

papers.title: Synthetic diet feeding exacerbates central nervous system autoimmunity in mice independent of weight gain
papers.abstract: Consumption of a nutrient deficient diet high in saturated fats and sugar is associated with the increased incidence and exacerbation of inflammatory and autoimmune diseases. Efforts to resolve the molecular mechanisms underlying diet-dependent changes to immune responses rely on the use of synthetic diets in mice, often using a standard laboratory chow as control. Critically, it remains unknown whether synthetic diet specific alterations in nutrient and metabolite availability, independent of weight gain and exposure to dietary fats and sugar, can affect the immune response. We reveal that exposure to a synthetic diet, independent of weight gain, is sufficient to alter the immune response, driving increased severity in the experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) model of central nervous system (CNS) autoimmunity. Mechanistically, synthetic diet feeding leads to systemic reductions in short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) abundance, and supplementation of synthetic diet with butyrate mitigates the excessive production of pathogenic T cells, and ameliorates synthetic diet driven increases in EAE severity. Finally, we identify the presence of peripheral Tregs (pTregs) in the CNS of EAE mice, which can arise from shared clonal ancestors as T helper (Th) cells, and reveal that butyrate supplementation increases the proportion pTregs to Th17 cells during EAE.

papers.title: Gas6 signaling via its cellular receptors is essential for homeostasis in response to endotoxemia and infection
papers.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome characterized by infection-induced organ dysfunction and dysregulated host inflammatory responses. Despite advances in supportive care, effective pharmacological therapies remain lacking. Growth arrest-specific protein 6 (Gas6), a vitamin K-dependent ligand of the TAM receptors (Tyro3, Axl, and Mer), operates at the interface of inflammation and coagulation. Here, we investigated the role of Gas6-TAM signaling in endotoxemia and infection in humans and mice. Plasma Gas6 levels increased rapidly during sepsis in patients, during experimental endotoxemia in both humans and mice, and during infection in mice, and these elevations correlated with disease severity and poor clinical outcomes. In both species, circulating Gas6 remained closely balanced with soluble Axl (sAxl), suggesting that much of plasma Gas6 is sequestered in soluble complexes, thereby limiting activation of membrane TAM receptors. In mice, deficiency of Gas6 or individual TAM receptors increased susceptibility to endotoxemia, and Gas6 deficiency additionally heightened vulnerability to bacterial infection. Gas6-deficient mice displayed reduced mean blood pressure, exaggerated cytokine release, altered early leukocyte dynamics, and enhanced macrophage activation. Mechanistically, macrophages secreted Gas6 in response to LPS, and Gas6 acted as an autocrine negative feedback signal limiting inflammatory cytokine production, at least in part through regulation of TLR signaling. Although Gas6 is strongly involved in immune regulation during sepsis, our data do not support a major direct role in coagulation activation. While circulating Gas6 and soluble Mer levels in septic patients were associated with sepsis-induced coagulopathy and impaired thrombin generation, this likely reflects disease severity rather than a causal effect on the coagulation. Consistently, in a murine endotoxemia model, Gas6 deficiency resulted in only minor changes in coagulation markers and did not lead to disseminated intravascular coagulation, suggesting that Gas6 primarily reflects systemic inflammation rather than directly driving coagulation abnormalities.

papers.title: Development of lentiviral vectors specifically targeting CD4+ cells
papers.abstract: Because of their central role in immunity, CD4+ T cells are a key target for genetic modification in many therapeutic applications, and lentiviral vectors with a VSV-G envelope are often used for this engineering. However, due to their broad tropism, these vectors are inadequate for cell-targeted in vivo gene delivery. Here, we explored using HIV-1 Env, which has a natural tropism towards these cells, as an alternative. We describe a three-plasmid vector production system to incorporate a panel of CCR5- or CXCR4-tropic Envs. These Env proteins are expressed from pCAG, a plasmid with reduced HIV-1 elements. We identify HIV-1 Env-incorporating vectors that can be produced with sufficient titres to specifically transduce primary CD4+ T cells in the context of in vitro mixed populations of peripheral blood mononuclear cells. We show efficient and specific transduction of HIV-1 Env vectors delivering an anti-CD19 chimeric antigen receptor (CAR). We demonstrate functional activity of the generated CD4+ CAR T cells, leading to the targeted killing of B cells in those mixed cell populations. Our methodology enables the production of HIV-1 Env-incorporating lentiviral vectors with defined CD4 targeted delivery, opening avenues for direct in vivo CAR T cell generation.

papers.title: A Senescence-Like State is associated with the Immunosuppressive Phenotype of Tumor-Infiltrating Regulatory T Cells
papers.abstract: Regulatory T (Treg) cells are essential mediators of immune suppression within the tumor microenvironment (TME) and represent a major barrier to effective anti-tumor immunity and to therapeutic efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Cellular senescence is traditionally characterized by stable cell-cycle arrest accompanied by distinct molecular and functional changes, yet whether tumor-infiltrating (TI) Treg cells acquire senescence-associated features and how these features influence their immunosuppressive activity remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that TI-Treg cells exhibit both apoptosis- and senescence-associated phenotype while retaining, and in some cases likely enhancing, their immunosuppressive capacity. Compared with peripheral Treg cells, some TI-Treg cells from solid cancers display elevated canonical senescence-associated markers, including p16 and p21, DNA damage response pathways, senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) and anti-apoptotic BCL-2 family genes, as well as activation of secretion associated beta-galactosidase (SA-beta-Gal). Though physiological Treg senescence leads to diminished immune suppression, TI-Treg cells paradoxically maintain the expression of key immunosuppressive molecules. These findings identify a previously unrecognized senescence-like state in TI-Treg cells that is functionally distinct from the loss of fitness typically associated with senescence in other cell types or aging-associated Treg senescence. Our study establishes senescence-associated reprogramming as a defining feature of TI-Treg cells and highlights the senescence-like state of Treg cells as a potential therapeutic target for selectively disrupting tumor immune suppression while preserving systemic immune homeostasis.

papers.title: Redox-driven control of 4-1BB interactome and signaling
papers.abstract: 4-1BB (CD137/TNFRSF9) is a major immunoregulatory receptor, yet the molecular principles governing its intracellular signaling remain unclear. Here we show that the conserved cytoplasmic cysteine residues of 4-1BB are critical determinants of its interactome, enabling redox-responsive engagement of TRAF2 and LANCL2. Using quantitative assays combined with mutational analysis, we redefine the TRAF2-binding region and show that mild oxidation induces a cysteine-dependent disulfide stabilization of the complex. We identify that 4-1BB interacts with GPX1 independently of LANCL2, most likely indirectly via TRAF2, providing local antioxidant support when glutathione (GSH) is sufficient, whereas LANCL2, whose binding competes with GSH, is favored under mildly oxidative conditions. 4-1BB signaling was found to alter cellular redox balance, in which both TRAF2 and LANCL2 sites are critical. These findings reveal that 4-1BB functions as a redox-sensitive interaction hub, switching between distinct signaling states depending on intracellular redox conditions and the cysteine-dependent remodeling of its protein interactions.

papers.title: Chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy targeting CD94 for cytotoxic T/NK cell malignancies
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy against pan-B-cell antigens is highly effective, but analogous approaches for T-cell lymphomas risk prolonged T-cell aplasia. We developed a CAR-T therapy targeting a post-thymic antigen, CD94, a receptor with restricted expression in normal tissues and immune cells but enriched in cytotoxic T/NK-cell malignancies. Second generation CD94 CAR T cells generated using a specific and high-affinity anti-CD94 monoclonal antibody showed potent and selective cytotoxicity against CD94-positive tumor cells in vitro and completely eradicated NK-cell leukemia xenografts and patient-derived xenograft models of hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma and NK/T-cell lymphoma in vivo. Incorporation of truncated B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) as a safety switch enabled rapid elimination of CAR T cells using anti-BCMA T-cell engagers or anti-BCMA antibody-drug conjugate. Super-resolution microscopy demonstrated intracellular sequestration of CD94 by the CAR, preventing fratricide. Collectively, these findings support anti-CD94 CAR-T therapy as a promising and novel treatment for cytotoxic T/NK-cell neoplasms.

papers.title: Nlrp6-dependent sentinel goblet cell functions dictate defensive responses during bacterial invasion of colonic crypts
papers.abstract: The intestinal mucus layer serves as the primary physical barrier against microbial invasion, shielding the epithelium from luminal pathogens and inflammatory insults. This barrier is maintained by a heterogeneous population of goblet cells (GCs), which secrete regionally and organizationally distinct mucus layers. However, when this primary barrier is compromised, the burden of defense likely shifts to secondary mechanisms that remain incompletely defined. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the proposed role of microbe-sensing sentinel goblet cells (senGCs) as a secondary defensive mechanism that becomes critical when the primary mucus barrier fails, focusing on their capacity to mount localized secretory responses and preserve crypt sterility under challenge conditions. Using a GC specific Nlrp6 knockout model (Nlrp6{Delta}GC), we demonstrate that senGC deficiency leads to increased susceptibility to DSS induced colitis and Citrobacter rodentium infection, marked by exacerbated inflammation and enhanced crypt invasion respectively. Transcriptomic and immunolgical profiling revealed both common and sex-specific immune dysregulation, with especially female Nlrp6{Delta}GC mice exhibiting heightened mucosal pathogen burden, reduced Th17 expansion and increased CD8 T cell recruitment. The senGC-deficient mice also showed diminished baseline mucus secretion and accelerated GC loss during infection, suggesting a previously unrecognized mucus maintenance role for senGCs. Furthermore, infection induced expansion of Nlrp6 GCs in wild-type mice, enhancing MAMP-triggered mucus secretion, a response that is absent in Nlrp6{Delta}GC tissue. These findings confirm senGCs as an important regulator of epithelial protection by integrating GC-intrinsic microbial sensing with mucosal defense.

papers.title: Repeated exposure to a conserved antigen drives dynamic clonal and epitope succession
papers.abstract: Defining the dynamics of T cell memory formation with epitope-level resolution can inform vaccine design. Longitudinal T cell receptor (TCR) sequencing after COVID-19 mRNA vaccination has enabled detailed tracking of T cell responses; however, connecting expanded clonotypes following antigen exposure to their cognate epitopes remains a challenge due to limited curated paired /{beta}TCR information. To fill this gap, we used TIRTL-seq to identify paired /{beta}TCRs from CD8+ T cell lineages associated with mRNA immunization in serial samples across 38 healthy donors over multiple rounds of vaccinations. Vaccine-associated paired /{beta}TCRs, identified based on their longitudinal kinetics, were grouped according to sequence similarity to infer their shared epitope specificities. We assigned epitope specificity to 1,109 clonotypes, recognizing 15 SARS-CoV-2 spike targets, identifying multiple previously undescribed responses, and confirming putative specificities experimentally. This approach uncovered a striking pattern of clonal succession in anti-spike T cell memory lineages resulting from repeated vaccination, characterized by a transition from low-avidity clones recognizing conserved coronavirus epitopes to high-avidity clones targeting epitopes unique to SARS-CoV-2. These results highlight the surprisingly dynamic responses underlying homologous boosting, suggest avenues for improving vaccine strategies, and pave the way for repertoire-based monitoring of antigen-specific T cell immunity.

papers.title: AlphaScreen profiling of extracellular vesicle-associated platelet, immune, and vascular markers reveals disease-specific signatures in ME/CFS, fibromyalgia, and long COVID
papers.abstract: Introduction: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS), fibromyalgia (FM), and long COVID (LC-19) are chronic diseases with overlapping clinical features and poorly understood pathophysiology. Increasing evidence suggests the involvement of immune dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, and altered vascular physiology. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are key mediators of intercellular communication and are envisioned as sensors of homeostasis and disease. The aim of this study was to determine whether EV marker profiling could provide a basis for the differential diagnosis of ME/CFS, FM and LC-19 and/or patient stratification. Methods: EV-enriched plasma from ME/CFS, FM, cases co-diagnosed with ME/CFS and FM, LC-19 patients, and matched healthy controls (n = 10 per study group) were analyzed. EV concentration and size distribution were assessed by nanoparticle tracking analysis, followed by targeted profiling of EV-associated surface markers via AlphaScreen, including tetraspanins CD9 and CD63, platelet- (CD41/CD61), myeloid- (CD13), immune- (CD74 and CX3CR1), and renin-angiotensin system- associated ACE1 (also known as CD143), and ACE2 surface markers. Results: The studied disease groups presented distinct EV signatures. LC-19 samples exhibited the most pronounced and coordinated alterations, characterized by increased levels of CD9/CD74, CD9/CX3CR1, and CD9/ACE1-positive EVs, along with reduced overall particle concentrations. Notably, platelet-derived CD9/CD41/CD61-positive EVs were significantly elevated in both LC-19 and ME/CFS, as compared to healthy controls, indicating enhanced platelet activation. Immune-associated markers revealed differential pathway activation in LC-19, with CD74-positive EVs reflecting antigen presentation and inflammatory signaling, and CX3CR1-positive EVs indicating altered leukocyte trafficking and vascular interaction. Increased ACE1-positive EVs in LC-19 further suggested a shift toward pro-inflammatory renin-angiotensin signaling. Conclusion: Collectively, these findings support a disease-specific dysregulation of platelet, immune, and vascular pathways. The integrated EV signatures distinguish LC-19 from the related chronic conditions ME/CFS and FM, highlighting the potential of EV-based profiling for differential diagnosis. Our results provide a systems-level perspective on the differential pathophysiology of these disorders and identify EV-associated markers as candidate biomarkers with clinical value.

papers.title: L-selectin shedding regulates post-infarction neutrophilia without altering myocardial injury or ventricular remodelling.
papers.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers rapid neutrophil mobilisation from the bone marrow (BM), resulting in systemic neutrophilia that is widely associated with myocardial injury. However, whether the magnitude of this response directly influences cardiac injury and subsequent ventricular remodelling remains unclear. Ectodomain shedding of L-selectin is a hallmark of neutrophil activation, although its contribution to neutrophil mobilisation following MI has not been established. Using mice expressing a non-cleavable L-selectin mutant (L(E)), we investigated the role of L-selectin shedding in post-MI neutrophilia. Under homeostatic conditions, WT and L(E) mice exhibited comparable BM neutrophil maturation and circulating neutrophil representation. Following permanent coronary ligation, however, L(E) mice exhibited markedly attenuated neutrophilia, associated with reduced circulating CXCL2 and decreased surface CXCR2 expression on BM neutrophils. Intravenous recombinant CXCL2 increased circulating neutrophil representation in WT but not L(E) mice, suggesting that impaired mobilisation cannot be explained solely by reduced ligand availability. Despite attenuated neutrophilia, myocardial neutrophil representation was comparable between genotypes at 24 hours post-MI. Circulating cardiac troponin I concentrations and MRI-quantified infarct size also showed no detectable differences. Longitudinal cardiac MRI at days 1, 14 and 28 revealed comparable ventricular structure and function, while histological scar size was similar at day 28. These findings identify L-selectin shedding as a regulator of post-MI neutrophilia and suggest that the magnitude of this systemic response can be dissociated from acute myocardial injury and subsequent ventricular remodelling.

papers.title: Dual cellular targeting of complement receptor 2 (CR2/CD21) synergistically suppresses autoreactive germinal center activity and autoimmunity in lupus
papers.abstract: Pathogenic germinal center (GC) activity persists in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) because current B cell-targeting therapies do not consistently eliminate the resilient GC niche that sustains autoimmunity. Complement receptor 2 (CR2/CD21) presents a unique bicellular therapeutic target to impede GC-associated autoimmune disease. For B cells, it has been previously shown to lower the threshold for B cell activation, and for follicular dendritic cells (FDCs), it sustains the GC response. Using a CD21-blocking antibody in a spontaneous lupus-prone mouse model, we demonstrate that dual CD21 blockade on both B cells and FDCs synergistically inhibited GC B cell responses and suppressed autoantibody production, memory recall, and renal antibody deposition. Mechanistically, B cell-specific blockade impaired GC entry by limiting initial activation, whereas FDC-specific blockade disrupted GC architecture and curtailed ongoing responses. Further, dual blockade uniquely reshaped immunological memory by promoting accumulation of a CD21low/-CD38+ memory B cell subset with attenuated antibody-secreting cell (ASC) recall potential. These findings identify CD21 blockade as a precision immunomodulatory strategy capable of suppressing pathogenic humoral immunity without complete B cell depletion.

papers.title: Selective Elimination of HIV-1-Infected Macrophages by Targeted Activator of Cell Kill
papers.abstract: In the pursuit of an HIV cure, elimination of persistent HIV reservoirs requires strategies that promote immune-mediated or cytopathic clearance of infected cells. While many such approaches are being developed against infected CD4+ T cells, HIV-infected macrophages are comparatively resistant to cell death and to several killing mechanisms being explored for T-cell reservoirs, highlighting the need for strategies that specifically eliminate this reservoir. Targeted Activator of Cell Kill (TACK), developed by Merck Pharmaceuticals, are non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor-derived molecules designed to selectively kill HIV-1-infected cells by inducing premature activation of the viral protease. Here, we evaluated the TACK compounds Pyr01 and it?s inactive analog Pyr02, in primary human monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs). Pyr01 had minimal effects on uninfected MDM viability but potently targeted HIV-1-infected MDMs, with an EC?? of approximately 0.36 ?M. Pyr01 treatment produced a rapid and sustained reduction in extracellular virion-associated HIV-1 RNA and significantly decreased cell-associated viral RNA, whereas Pyr02 exhibited minimal activity. Immunofluorescence microscopy and live-cell imaging further demonstrated a marked loss of HIV-1-infected macrophages following Pyr01 treatment, consistent with selective elimination of infected cells. These findings identify Pyr01 as a specific mediator of HIV-infected macrophage death and establish premature viral protease activation as a strategy for overcoming the intrinsic resistance of macrophage reservoirs to clearance. Targeting this macrophage-specific barrier may complement approaches directed at CD4+ T-cell reservoirs and broaden the cellular reach of HIV cure strategies.

papers.title: Exploratory positional differences in observed CDRH2 lineage-state transitions following HIV-1 germline-targeting vaccination
papers.abstract: Background: Germline-targeting HIV-1 vaccination recruits VRC01-class B-cell precursors, but the positional patterns of observed longitudinal B-cell receptor lineage-state changes remain incompletely described. We compared CDRH2 profiles between homologous and heterologous boosting regimens using published IAVI G002 data. Methods: Participant-specific Week-8 lineages were prospectively matched to Week-24 observations. Germline-to-nongermline changes in sampled lineage-modal residues were evaluated at seven IGHV1-2*02 CDRH2 positions using participant-balanced, mean-centered profiles and exact participant-label permutation inference. Sampling-depth and sorting-probe sensitivity analyses assessed observability. A separate participant-held-out benchmark evaluated antibody-language-model representations for predicting observed Week-24 lineage detection. Results: The CDRH2 analysis included 332 lineages, 15 participants, 2,179 eligible lineage-position observations, and 241 observed state changes. The regional profile statistic was 0.027066 (exact p = 0.001709; six-region adjusted q = 0.010256), with descriptive differences at V-relative positions 51, 54, and 55. Most eligible longitudinal observations had one assessable cell per visit. In seven Group-1 participants, Week-24 dual-probe sampling recovered 181 baseline lineages with eOD-GT8 and 143 with Cg28v2, including 60 detected by both probes. In a separate cohort of 2,739 lineages from 17 participants, IgBERT and AbLang-2 representations did not improve participant-balanced average precision over a four-feature biological baseline. Conclusions: Observed CDRH2 lineage-modal-state profiles differed between regimens in this exploratory secondary analysis. Sparse sampling, potentially probe-related ascertainment, and absent linked functional validation preclude inference about mutation timing, functional improvement, or causal booster effects.

papers.title: COVID-19 and Active Tuberculosis Exhibit Distinct Maturation-Associated Neutrophil Transcriptional Programs
papers.abstract: Neutrophils can promote pathogen control or drive tissue-damaging inflammation, but the mechanisms that determine these divergent outcomes remain poorly defined. COVID-19 and active tuberculosis (TB) offer a purposeful comparison since both are pulmonary infections with substantial neutrophil involvement, yet differ in pathogen class, inflammatory duration, and the balance between neutrophil-associated host defense and pathology. We therefore tested whether their divergent neutrophil programs align with distinct maturation-associated transcriptional states. We integrated six publicly available whole-blood bulk RNA-sequencing datasets, comprising three COVID-19 and three active TB cohorts. A curated panel of 770 genes covered activation, degranulation, neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, chemotaxis, cell surface receptors, and maturation. Study-associated variation was reduced using ComBat-Seq, and differential expression relative to disease-appropriate controls was assessed with DESeq2. Most genes changed in the same direction in both diseases, but 348 (45.2%) differed significantly in response magnitude, with 159 genes showing a stronger response in COVID-19 and 189 in TB. COVID-19 samples showed reduced expression of the maturation markers CD10 (MME) and CD16 (FCGR3A), alongside elevated expression of granule-cargo and NET-associated genes, including MPO and ELANE, consistent with a greater contribution from immature, emergency granulopoiesis-derived neutrophil populations. In contrast, TB samples showed higher maturation-associated, receptor, oxidative, and recruitment responses, consistent with a relatively mature receptor-competent neutrophil transcriptional signature. Independent COVID-19 Ward and pulmonary TB cohorts showed directional agreement for maturation and NET-associated signatures (100% and 90% concordance, respectively), while chemotaxis and select receptor and degranulation genes showed weaker reproducibility indicating that maturation represents the most consistently reproduced axis of distinction between the two diseases. Together, these findings identify maturation-associated transcription as the most consistently reproduced axis distinguishing COVID-19 from TB. These signatures provide candidate biomarkers for future studies linking neutrophil states to clinical outcomes and informing host-directed therapeutic strategies that preserve antimicrobial function while limiting immunopathology.

papers.title: T cell receptors from CD8 regulatory T cells direct the development of natural intraepithelial lymphocytes
papers.abstract: CD8 regulatory T cells (CD8 Tregs) in mice have been identified by their expression of the surface receptor family Ly49 and the transcription factor Helios. To our surprise, many Ly49+ and Helios+ T cells express neither CD4 nor CD8, and many express only CD8. We found that CD8 Tregs in the spleen are linked to the CD8{beta}- natural intraepithelial lymphocytes (IELs) that reside in the small intestine. Blocking trafficking to the intestine increased splenic CD8 Treg frequency, and transferred splenic CD8 Tregs gave rise to natural IELs. Unexpectedly, Helios was dispensable for natural IEL development, arguing against its role as a shared lineage-determining transcription factor. Instead, we found that T cell receptors (TCRs) from splenic Ly49+ CD8 Tregs deterministically direct natural IEL development. Our findings suggest that CD8 Tregs may derive from the same TCR-directed developmental program that generates natural IELs and shed light on the origins of these immunoregulatory cells.
